ruleName: Order of Play in Stroke Play
imagePrompt: A polished, modern, semi-realistic (about 75% realistic and 25% stylised) illustration in a vibrant junior golf quiz style. The scene shows a putting green with a visible hole and flagstick. One golfer stands on the green near their ball, which is farther from the hole. A second golfer is preparing to play from a nearby greenside bunker. The ball in the bunker is clearly closer to the hole than the ball on the green. The image should show the distance difference between the positions, both balls, both players ready to play, and the whole setting should be easily recognisable as a golf course. Do not include any text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards, or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: One golfer is on the putting green standing near their ball, which is farther from the hole, while another golfer is in a bunker preparing to play a ball that is closer to the hole.

sceneSpec.setting: Putting green and adjacent greenside bunker
sceneSpec.players: Two golfers: one preparing to putt, one preparing to play from a bunker
sceneSpec.ballPosition: One ball on the putting green, farther from the hole; one ball in a greenside bunker, closer to the hole
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: Deciding who plays first based on distance from the hole
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Illustrates that order of play depends on distance from hole, not where the ball lies
mustShow: Golf hole with visible flagstick on putting green
One golfer near their ball on the green, looking toward the hole
One golfer in a bunker preparing to play their ball
The ball on the green is farther from the hole than the ball in the bunker
Clear visual distance difference between the two balls

questions.title: Who goes first if one ball is on the green and the other is in a bunker closer to the hole?
questions.question: You are playing golf with a friend. Your ball is on the green, but not very close to the hole. Your friend's ball is in the sand bunker, but the bunker is a bit closer to the hole than your ball. Who should take their shot first?

choices.text: You should go first because your ball is on the green.
Your friend should go first because their ball is farther from the hole.
Your friend should go first because their ball is farther from the hole.
You can choose who goes first.

questions.explanation: In stroke play, the player whose ball is farthest from the hole always plays first, no matter if it is on the green, in the sand, or on the grass. In this case, your ball is farther away, so you go first.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The smooth grass near the hole where you putt the ball.
A sandy area on the golf course, also called a sand trap.
A type of golf game where you count every shot you take during a round.

questions.teachingTip: Ask the children to look at where each ball is and which one is farthest from the hole. Remind them it doesn't matter if the ball is on the green, in a bunker, or on the grass.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking the player on the green should always play first.
Believing the player in the bunker must always go last.

questions.title: Who plays first when one ball is on the green and another in a bunker closer to the hole?
questions.question: In a stroke play competition, your ball is on the putting green. Your playing partner's ball is in a bunker, but it is closer to the hole than yours. Who should play first?

choices.text: You should play first because your ball is already on the putting green.
Your partner should play first because their ball is farther from the hole.
Your partner should play first because their ball is farther from the hole.
You can choose who plays first.

questions.explanation: The order of play in stroke play is determined by which ball is farther from the hole, not by which area of the course the ball is in. Even if one ball is on the green and another elsewhere, the player whose ball is farther away plays first. Ready Golf is encouraged in stroke play to improve pace of play, but there is no penalty for playing out of turn. In this scenario, since your ball is on the green and your partner's ball is in a bunker closer to the hole, you (with the ball farther from the hole) should play first.
